models – the ORM mapping and the Engine

The applicants table as SQLAlchemy sees it, and the lazily built Engine cache that lets one environment variable redirect every query the application makes.

SQLAlchemy 2.x mapping of the applicants table, plus the Engine and Session.

This is the same table load_data writes with psycopg and query_data reads with raw SQL – there is exactly one copy of the data. The model is declared against the existing schema rather than owning it: the loader is what creates the table, and Base.metadata here simply describes what is already there so the ORM can read and write it.

orm_queries and flask_app both get their Sessions from here.

The Engine is built on first use, not on import. Module 3 created it at import time, which meant the process was bound to whatever DATABASE_URL said the moment the first module imported this one – so a test could not point the ORM at a scratch database without reloading the module. get_engine() instead caches one Engine per URL and reset_engine() throws the cache away, which is all a fixture needs to redirect every query in the application.

python models.py # check the mapping against the live database

models.REQUIRED_FIELDS = ('p_id', 'program', 'comments', 'date_added', 'url', 'status', 'term', 'us_or_international', 'gpa', 'gre', 'gre_v', 'gre_aw', 'degree', 'llm_generated_program', 'llm_generated_university')

The columns the assignment’s schema requires, in order. Everything that reads or writes a whole applicant row – the loader, the query helpers, the schema tests – names its fields from this one tuple, so a column added in one place cannot go missing in another.

models.database_url()[source]

Build the SQLAlchemy URL from the same environment psycopg uses.

URL.create rather than a formatted string, so a password containing @, / or # is escaped correctly instead of silently splitting the URL. The postgresql+psycopg driver name selects psycopg 3, matching the adapter the rest of the application uses.

Return type:

URL

class models.Applicant(**kwargs)[source]

Bases: Base

One Grad Cafe admissions result.

Column names and types mirror the assignment’s schema exactly. p_id is the Grad Cafe result id, which makes it a natural primary key: it is stable across scrapes, so re-loading the same entry updates its row rather than adding another. That is the uniqueness policy the idempotency tests check.

Everything except p_id is nullable, because Grad Cafe entries are self-submitted and most of them leave the optional fields blank – roughly 41% report a GPA and under 8% report any GRE score.

p_id: Mapped[int]
program: Mapped[str | None]

as_dict()[source]

This row as a plain dict keyed by REQUIRED_FIELDS.

What the Flask layer and the query helpers hand around, so nothing outside this module has to know it is holding a mapped instance whose Session may since have closed.

Return type:

Dict[str, Any]

models.get_engine()[source]

The Engine for the current environment, created once per URL.

Keyed on the rendered URL rather than on nothing at all, so a test that repoints DATABASE_URL gets its own Engine and connection pool instead of one still bound to the previous database.

Return type:

Engine

models.reset_engine()[source]

Dispose of every cached Engine and forget it.

Called by the test fixtures between databases, and worth having in production too: it is the only way to make the application let go of a connection pool without restarting the process.

Return type:

None

models.get_sessionmaker()[source]

A configured Session factory bound to the current Engine.

expire_on_commit=False so a row read inside session_scope() is still readable after the commit that closed the Session – the Flask layer reads answers out of one and renders them after it has gone.

Return type:

sessionmaker

models.get_session()[source]

One new Session, for a caller that will close it itself.

Return type:

Session

models.session_scope()[source]

Yield a Session that is committed on success and rolled back on error.

Return type:

Iterator[Session]

models.main()[source]

Confirm the mapping lines up with the live table.

Return type:

int
